project.name: Q017 · How is immune homeostasis maintained and regulated?
project.question: Immune homeostasis is a state of internal equilibrium. Without homeostasis, the immune system cannot function correctly, leading to disease and infection. Knowing how this balance is maintained can provide a fuller picture of how the body works and may help us in calibrating medical interventions. For instance, instead of nonselectively boosting or suppressing the whole immune system as we currently do, in the future we may be able to rebalance a dysregulated immune system. Studies in humans and in animal models have pursued almost every aspect of immune response and examined many immune cell populations, yet several unanswered questions remain. Genomic, proteomic, and other ‘omics data are helpful. But the human immune system is dynamic and very individualized, making animal models of limited use—thus a robust platform to study and manipulate human immune cells is needed to address the problem.

payload.title: Human immune-cell perturbation platform
payload.rationale: Establishes a high-fidelity ex vivo and organoid-based experimental framework to directly manipulate human immune networks, bypassing species-specific translational gaps inherent in animal models.
payload.completion_test: A validated standard operating procedure for multi-parameter single-cell readouts post-perturbation, complete with dose-response matrices, viability controls, and predefined success thresholds for signaling fidelity.
payload.remaining: IRB clearance, patient sample procurement, and bench-scale protocol validation.

brief.title: Human Immune-Cell Perturbation Platform Handoff: B-Cell Organoid & Epigenetic Modulation Focus
learned: Synthetic hydrogel-based lymphoid organoids can successfully sustain germinal center reactions and model human B-cell programming.
PBMC-derived constructs demonstrate potential longevity advantages over tonsil-derived equivalents for maintaining plasma cell populations.
Concurrent chemical inhibition of EZH2 and BCL6 is hypothesized to synergistically drive terminal plasma cell differentiation beyond single-target blockade.
The current evidence base is fragmented, consisting primarily of publication metadata, paywalled abstracts, and extraction failures rather than validated experimental protocols.
evidence: Qualitatively supports the use of engineered hydrogels to mimic lymphoid microenvironments for controlled B-cell response modeling.
Demonstrates differential therapeutic responses (e.g., anti-CD20 impairment) and microenvironmental sensitivity between healthy donors and lymphoma patients.
Validates the technical feasibility of multi-parameter mass cytometry and transcriptomic profiling to track hematopoietic continuum dynamics post-perturbation.
Indicates that targeted epigenetic/transcriptional modulation can influence germinal center architecture and plasma cell output in vitro.
limitations: Cannot substantiate comprehensive immune network manipulation due to a narrow focus on B-cells and absence of T-cell/innate lymphoid data.
Lacks the validated standard operating procedures, dose-response matrices, viability controls, and predefined signaling fidelity thresholds mandated by the completion test.
Fails to account for donor-to-donor immunological variability, ex vivo expansion artifacts, and potential off-target cytotoxicity without empirical wet-lab execution.
Dry-lab simulations and computational models cannot replicate the complex biophysical constraints of hydrogel matrices or real-time epigenetic-transcriptional crosstalk.
open_questions: What are the precise molar ratios and dosing kinetics for concurrent EZH2/BCL6 inhibition that maximize synergy while maintaining >60% cell viability?
How does inter-donor variability impact organoid reproducibility, and what statistical power metrics are required to normalize survival curves?
Can polarized CXCL12 gradients or other microenvironmental cues overcome anti-CD20-induced suppression in lymphoma-derived B-cell niches?
Which specific multi-parameter readouts and viability-correction algorithms best define 'signaling fidelity' across heterogeneous primary isolates?
next_moves: Secure IRB approval and procure matched healthy/lymphoma donor peripheral blood mononuclear cells for cohort expansion.
Develop and internally validate the wet-lab SOP, establishing titrated dose-response matrices, vehicle controls, and standardized viability normalization protocols.
Execute bench-scale hydrogel organoid cultures with EZH2/BCL6 perturbations, capturing multi-parameter flow cytometry and transcriptomic endpoints.
Apply formal synergy quantification models (Bliss Independence, Chou-Talalay) and pre-study power calculations to generate definitive success thresholds.
Temporarily narrow the directional scope to B-cell lymphoid organoids pending acquisition of broader immune network validation data.

findings.recommendation: Retrieve full-text versions or substitute with accessible primary literature detailing wet-lab SOPs, dose-response validation, and multi-parameter single-cell readout protocols to substantiate the proposed framework.

Narrow the directional scope to align with available evidence (e.g., B-cell lymphoid organoids and mass cytometry profiling) or acquire broader immunological perturbation data before claiming comprehensive immune network manipulation.
Develop and document the required SOP, dose-response matrices, and viability controls internally prior to submission, as current sources provide zero procedural validation or threshold definitions.

review.summary: The proposed human immune-cell perturbation platform relies on fragmented, inaccessible, or erroneous source material. Available evidence consists primarily of publication metadata, a single extraction failure, and a paywalled abstract focusing narrowly on B-cell organoids. Consequently, the rationale overstates the breadth of applicable data, and the specified completion test (validated SOP with dose-response matrices and signaling thresholds) is entirely unsupported. Substantive full-text literature or internal experimental documentation is required to validate the workflow and adjust the scope accordingly.

## Human immune organoids to decode B cell response in healthy donors and patients with lymphoma | Nature Materials

**Source**: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-024-02037-1

---

[Skip to main content](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-024-02037-1?error=cookies_not_supported&code=d69e5d8a-9808-4353-a607-9c8e9f37a64e#content)

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up
to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles
and JavaScript.

## Abstract

Antibodies are produced when naive B cells differentiate into plasma cells within germinal centres (GCs) of lymphoid tissues. Patients with B cell lymphoma on
effective immunotherapies exhibit diminished antibody production, leading to higher infection rates and reduced vaccine efficacy, even after B cell recovery.
Current ex vivo models fail to sustain long-term GC reactions and effectively test B cell responses. Here we developed synthetic hydrogels mimicking the
lymphoid tissue microenvironment, enabling human GCs from tonsils and peripheral blood mononuclear cell-derived B cells. Immune organoids derived from
peripheral blood mononuclear cells maintain GC B cells and plasma cells longer than tonsil-derived ones and exhibit unique B cell programming, including GC
compartments, somatic hypermutation, immunoglobulin class switching and B cell clones. Chemical inhibition of transcriptional and epigenetic processes enhances
plasma cell formation. While integrating polarized CXCL12 protein in a lymphoid organ-on-chip modulates GC responses in healthy donor B cells, it fails with B
cells derived from patients with lymphoma. Our system allows rapid, controlled modelling of immune responses and B cell disorders.

protocol.hypothesis: Concurrent chemical inhibition of EZH2 and BCL6 in PBMC-derived hydrogel organoids will yield a statistically significant, viability-corrected increase in terminal plasma cell differentiation rates that mathematically exceeds the additive thresholds predicted by single-target epigenetic blockade alone.
protocol.samples: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) isolated from healthy adult donors, expanded ex vivo, and embedded in standardized synthetic PEG-fibrinogen hydrogels to form B-cell lymphoid organoids under defined germinal center induction conditions.
perturbations: Concurrent dual inhibition at matched molar ratios across the dose matrix
controls: Single-agent EZH2 inhibition at identical concentrations
Single-agent BCL6 inhibition at identical concentrations
Fresh primary PBMC baseline (day 0 viability and phenotype)
endpoints: Terminal plasma cell frequency (CD19- CD27high CD38high) via flow cytometry
Transcriptional output (PRDM1, XBP1, IRF4 mRNA/protein levels)
Phospho-signaling readouts for downstream BCR/TGF-beta pathways
protocol.analysis_plan: Generate full dose-response matrices for all perturbations. Normalize all differentiation endpoints to day-0 fresh isolates and correct for compound-induced cytotoxicity. Calculate synergy indices using Bliss Independence and Chou-Talalay models. Compare dual-inhibition outcomes against single-agent curves using two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni correction. Apply pre-study power calculations to confirm statistical significance before finalizing conclusions.
stopping_rules: Terminate experiment if overall viability drops below 60% at any timepoint
Abort dose escalation if IC50 shifts indicate non-specific membrane disruption
Cease cohort expansion if donor-matched variability exceeds predefined CV thresholds (>15%)
Stop if no measurable GC structure forms by day 7 regardless of treatment
safety_and_ethics: IRB-approved informed consent for human peripheral blood collection
Adherence to BSL-2 laboratory practices for human cell culture
Proper handling and disposal of cytotoxic small-molecule inhibitors per institutional EHS guidelines
De-identification of all donor samples and compliance with HIPAA/GDPR data protection standards
protocol.cannot_establish_without_execution: Computational environments and dry-lab simulations cannot replicate the complex biophysical constraints of hydrogel matrices, dynamic cytokine gradients, or real-time epigenetic-transcriptional crosstalk required to validate synergistic plasma cell differentiation; empirical wet-lab execution with multi-parameter single-cell readouts is strictly necessary.

learned: Synthetic hydrogel-based lymphoid organoids can successfully sustain germinal center reactions and model human B-cell programming.
PBMC-derived constructs demonstrate potential longevity advantages over tonsil-derived equivalents for maintaining plasma cell populations.
Concurrent chemical inhibition of EZH2 and BCL6 is hypothesized to synergistically drive terminal plasma cell differentiation beyond single-target blockade.
The current evidence base is fragmented, consisting primarily of publication metadata, paywalled abstracts, and extraction failures rather than validated experimental protocols.
evidence: Qualitatively supports the use of engineered hydrogels to mimic lymphoid microenvironments for controlled B-cell response modeling.
Demonstrates differential therapeutic responses (e.g., anti-CD20 impairment) and microenvironmental sensitivity between healthy donors and lymphoma patients.
Validates the technical feasibility of multi-parameter mass cytometry and transcriptomic profiling to track hematopoietic continuum dynamics post-perturbation.
Indicates that targeted epigenetic/transcriptional modulation can influence germinal center architecture and plasma cell output in vitro.
limitations: Cannot substantiate comprehensive immune network manipulation due to a narrow focus on B-cells and absence of T-cell/innate lymphoid data.
Lacks the validated standard operating procedures, dose-response matrices, viability controls, and predefined signaling fidelity thresholds mandated by the completion test.
Fails to account for donor-to-donor immunological variability, ex vivo expansion artifacts, and potential off-target cytotoxicity without empirical wet-lab execution.
Dry-lab simulations and computational models cannot replicate the complex biophysical constraints of hydrogel matrices or real-time epigenetic-transcriptional crosstalk.
open_questions: What are the precise molar ratios and dosing kinetics for concurrent EZH2/BCL6 inhibition that maximize synergy while maintaining >60% cell viability?
How does inter-donor variability impact organoid reproducibility, and what statistical power metrics are required to normalize survival curves?
Can polarized CXCL12 gradients or other microenvironmental cues overcome anti-CD20-induced suppression in lymphoma-derived B-cell niches?
Which specific multi-parameter readouts and viability-correction algorithms best define 'signaling fidelity' across heterogeneous primary isolates?
next_moves: Secure IRB approval and procure matched healthy/lymphoma donor peripheral blood mononuclear cells for cohort expansion.
Develop and internally validate the wet-lab SOP, establishing titrated dose-response matrices, vehicle controls, and standardized viability normalization protocols.
Execute bench-scale hydrogel organoid cultures with EZH2/BCL6 perturbations, capturing multi-parameter flow cytometry and transcriptomic endpoints.
Apply formal synergy quantification models (Bliss Independence, Chou-Talalay) and pre-study power calculations to generate definitive success thresholds.
Temporarily narrow the directional scope to B-cell lymphoid organoids pending acquisition of broader immune network validation data.
